span: There is no explanation worth the name contained in the condonation of delay application
why: Court refuses to condone a 131-day delay beyond the 60-day statutory period for want of any explanation and dismisses the appeal; it treats power as conditional on sufficient cause.

span: this Court condoned the delay in filing the appeal as a large number of similarly situate persons have been granted relief by this Court
why: Describes an earlier case relied on by a party; the following paragraph says such decisions do not help, so the court does not adopt it.

span: Delay thus remained unexplained – Discretion was not exercised judiciously by the High Court – Order of High Court quashed.
why: Holding: the High Court's condonation of a 1011-day delay is quashed because no sufficient cause was shown.

span: the delay beyond the period of 60 days from the date of service of the assessment order on the respondent-assessee cannot be condoned
why: Describes the appellate authority's conclusion in the lower proceedings, which the Supreme Court is reviewing; not the Supreme Court's own holding here.

span: By and large a liberal approach is to be taken in the matter of condonation of delay
why: Holding affirms a liberal approach to condonation but says long delay is not condoned automatically and routine explanations are insufficient; the delay in the case was not condoned.

span: This explanation falls woefully short of making out any sufficient cause.
why: Court sets aside a condonation of delay and dismisses an appeal as time-barred for lack of sufficient cause.

span: Hence, sufficient cause for condoning the delay has been shown. The delay in filing the Special Leave Petitions is condoned.
why: Court gives reasons (pending review petition) and condones the delay in approaching it, affirming the power on sufficient cause.
